adds.name: The Church of St. Michael & St. George
adds.description: One of St. Louis’s most prominent Episcopal parishes, an English Gothic landmark on Wydown Boulevard designed by architect James P. Jamieson. It was formed in 1928 by the merger of St. Michael & All Angels (founded in Clayton, 1913) and St. George’s (founded in the City of St. Louis, 1845); the nave was later extended and the Jay Herndon Smith Memorial Tower links the church to its parish hall. The parish also runs the St. Michael School of Clayton (1969).

history.event: St. George’s Episcopal Church is established in the City of St. Louis.
St. Michael & All Angels begins in Clayton.
The two parishes merge to form The Church of St. Michael & St. George on Wydown Boulevard (architect James P. Jamieson).
The parish founds the St. Michael School of Clayton.

adds.name: The St. Michael School of Clayton
adds.description: An Episcopal parish day school (junior-kindergarten through grade 6) founded in 1969 by The Church of St. Michael & St. George, sharing the parish’s Wydown campus.

history.event: The Church of St. Michael & St. George founds the school for children of the parish and community.

adds.name: Hi-Pointe Lofts
adds.description: Loft-style apartments on Clayton Road at the Hi-Pointe/DeMun edge, near the McCausland commercial node and steps from Forest Park.

adds.name: The Cheshire
amenities: Literary-themed suites (Sherlock Holmes, Brideshead Revisited, Chronicles of Narnia…)
Fox & Hounds Tavern — candlelit English pub
Outdoor pool (direct room access on select suites)
7,000+ sq ft of event space across 6 venues
Steps from Forest Park & the Hi-Pointe Theatre
adds.description: A Tudor landmark on Clayton Road at the gateway to Forest Park, The Cheshire is a British-inspired boutique hotel of half-timbered gables and literary-themed suites — Sherlock Holmes, Brideshead Revisited, Chronicles of Narnia. A St. Louis icon since 1964 (as the Cheshire Inn) and reborn as a modern boutique hotel, it houses the candlelit Fox & Hounds Tavern, the Italian restaurant Basso, a Starbucks, an outdoor pool, and 7,000+ square feet of event space — a beloved wedding venue moments from the park and the Hi-Pointe Theatre.

history.event: The Cheshire Inn opens on Clayton Road — a Tudor, English-themed inn that becomes a St. Louis landmark at the edge of Forest Park, long known for its Fox & Hounds Tavern.
After a full renovation the property reopens as "The Cheshire," a boutique hotel of literary-themed suites, keeping the Fox & Hounds and adding the Italian restaurant Basso.

adds.name: Hi-Pointe Theatre
adds.opening_hours_raw: Showtimes vary — doors open 30 min before each screening (arrive 15 min early); box office by phone during business hours
amenities: Art Deco décor & the iconic neon marquee
Snacks & drinks welcome in the auditorium
Free evening/weekend parking (Lindell Bank lot across McCausland)
adds.description: The oldest continuously operating single-screen movie theater in the St. Louis area — built in 1922 on "the highest point in the City of St. Louis," and always meant for movies, never vaudeville. A beautifully preserved Art Deco house with an iconic neon marquee and a 414-seat auditorium, it screens 35mm film and 2K digital, pours local beer and wine, and runs a repertory-plus-independent program. Since 2023 it has been operated by the nonprofit Cinema St. Louis, carrying a 100-year tradition forward.

history.event: The Hi-Pointe Theatre opens at Clayton Road & McCausland — purpose-built for movies (not vaudeville or plays) on the highest point in the City of St. Louis.
Joins the St. Louis Amusement Co. chain; later operated by Fanchon & Marco and Arthur Enterprises.
The auditorium is refitted with its signature aquamarine seating.
The James family buys the Hi-Pointe and runs it for three generations — some 45 years — keeping the single screen alive through the multiplex era.
The nonprofit Cinema St. Louis acquires the theater just past its 100th birthday, preserving it as a repertory art house.

adds.name: The Dorchester on Forest Park
adds.description: A 23-story luxury apartment tower on South Skinker Boulevard, perched between Forest Park and the DeMun neighborhood — one of the tallest residences on the park’s western edge, with sweeping views over the park and Washington University.

adds.name: 625 South Skinker Condominium
adds.description: A stately pre-war apartment building on South Skinker Boulevard overlooking Forest Park, now operated as a condominium — part of the boulevard’s celebrated row of 1920s "grand apartments" at the park’s edge.

adds.name: Central Seventh-day Adventist Church
adds.description: A Seventh-day Adventist congregation on North Skinker Boulevard at the edge of Forest Park.

adds.name: Ralph M. Captain Elementary School
adds.description: A public elementary school in the School District of Clayton — a two-time National Blue Ribbon School (2015, 2024) that ranks among the top 5% in Missouri.

adds.name: Vedanta Society of St. Louis
adds.description: A Hindu temple and spiritual center on South Skinker Boulevard, a branch of the Ramakrishna Order of India, offering Sunday services, classes, meditation, study circles, retreats and lectures in a serene setting across from Forest Park.

history.event: The Vedanta Society of St. Louis is founded by Swami Satprakashananda, a monk of the Ramakrishna Order and disciple of Swami Brahmananda.

adds.name: Oak Knoll Park
adds.address: 1 Oak Knoll (Clayton Rd at Big Bend)
adds.description: A 14.5-acre Clayton park at Clayton Road and Big Bend, home to one of the region’s largest native stands of post oak and a pond with a lighted fountain and gardens. Two early-20th-century stone mansions on the grounds — once a natural-history museum (1959–1992, whose collection helped seed the St. Louis Science Center) — now house the Greater St. Louis Community Foundation and the Clayton Early Childhood Center.

history.event: Lawyer Charles Rice buys the land — part of the old 300-acre Kennedy Farm — and builds 1 Oak Knoll.
The City of Clayton establishes Oak Knoll Park (14.5 acres).
The Academy of Science installs part of its collection in the park’s stone mansions — a museum that runs until the collection moves toward the new St. Louis Science Center (1992).

anchor.address: 1 Oak Knoll (Clayton Rd at Big Bend)

adds.name: Clayton Child Center
adds.description: An early-childhood center serving Clayton families, set by Oak Knoll Park.

adds.name: Millbrook Apartment 3
adds.description: Part of the Millbrook — a cluster of 1920s-era brick apartment buildings in the DeMun neighborhood (Millbrook Apartment 3).

adds.name: The Versailles Condominium
adds.description: One of the grand 1920s apartment buildings facing Forest Park along South Skinker Boulevard, built as luxury apartments and converted to a 45-unit condominium in 1980 — a classic of the boulevard’s stately pre-war residential wall.

history.event: The Versailles converts from luxury apartments to a 45-unit condominium (declaration recorded January 1981).

adds.name: Millbrook Apartment 1
adds.description: Part of the Millbrook — a cluster of 1920s-era brick apartment buildings in the DeMun neighborhood (Millbrook Apartment 1).

adds.name: Stevenson's Hi-Pointe Amoco
adds.opening_hours_raw: Open daily — fuel, convenience & auto service
amenities: Home of the World's Largest Amoco Sign — 40 ft × 60 ft, 44 tons of steel
5,800 bulbs · 2,900 ft of neon tubing · 5 miles of wiring
Illuminated at night — a beacon visible across Forest Park
adds.description: Home of the World's Largest Amoco Sign — a 40-by-60-foot, 44-ton neon beacon (5,800 bulbs, 2,900 feet of tubing, five miles of wiring) that has towered over the Skinker–Clayton–Oakland triangle at the edge of Forest Park since 1961. Fuel has been sold on this lot since Standard Oil bought the triangle in 1921; L.C. Stevenson opened the current station in 1951, and the family-run Stevenson's Hi-Pointe Amoco still pumps gas beneath the sign. One of St. Louis's most beloved roadside icons, refreshed in 2019 with new colors and energy-efficient lighting.

history.event: Standard Oil (John D. Rockefeller's company) buys the Skinker & Clayton triangle and erects its first double-sided Standard Oil sign.
A service station is added beneath the sign.
L.C. Stevenson opens the service station that still bears the family name.
The giant Amoco sign is raised — 44 tons of steel, 5,800 bulbs, 2,900 feet of neon tubing and five miles of wiring — the largest Amoco sign in the world.
The sign is refreshed with updated colors and energy-efficient lighting; Stevenson's Hi-Pointe Amoco keeps pumping beneath it.

adds.name: Memorial Presbyterian Church
adds.description: A Gothic-styled Presbyterian congregation on South Skinker Boulevard at the edge of Forest Park, near the Wash U campus.

adds.name: The Wilson School
adds.description: An independent, coeducational preparatory school (pre-K through grade 6) in the DeMun neighborhood — the oldest formalized early-childhood program in the St. Louis metro. Founded in 1913 by kindergarten pioneer Mabel Wilson as “Miss Wilson’s School” in her home; its landmark 1916 building was designed by noted school architect William B. Ittner.

history.event: Mabel Wilson founds “Miss Wilson’s School” in her St. Louis home — the metro’s first formalized early-childhood program.
Its historic building is designed by school-architecture pioneer William B. Ittner.
The Wilson School moves to its current DeMun/Clayton campus on Alamo Avenue.

adds.name: Wiltshire Condominium
adds.description: A South Skinker Boulevard apartment building facing Forest Park, now condominiums — another of the boulevard’s early-20th-century residential landmarks along the park.

adds.name: Wydown Middle School
adds.description: The School District of Clayton’s middle school on Wydown Boulevard, opened in 1936 in the former Hosmer Hall (a private girls’ school the district acquired).

history.event: The district opens Wydown by purchasing Hosmer Hall, a private girls’ school.

adds.school_type: Public middle school (School District of Clayton)

adds.name: Millbrook Apartment 4
adds.description: Part of the Millbrook — a cluster of 1920s-era brick apartment buildings in the DeMun neighborhood (Millbrook Apartment 4).

adds.name: Graham Chapel
adds.description: Washington University’s beloved Collegiate Gothic chapel, designed by Cope & Stewardson and completed in 1909 as the 12th building on the Danforth campus. Funded by Christine Blair Graham in memory of her husband Benjamin Graham (founder of the Graham Paper Company), its soaring nave, tracery windows and twin towers make it one of St. Louis’s favorite settings for concerts, ceremonies and weddings.

history.event: Christine Blair Graham offers to fund a university chapel in memory of her husband, Benjamin Graham.
Graham Memorial Chapel is completed — Collegiate Gothic Revival by Cope & Stewardson, the 12th building at Washington University.

adds.name: Wydown United Church
adds.description: A neighborhood United Church of Christ congregation on Wydown Boulevard in Clayton.

adds.name: Bethel Lutheran Church
adds.description: A Lutheran congregation on Wydown Boulevard in Clayton, near the Wash U campus.

adds.name: Millbrook Apartment 2
adds.description: Part of the Millbrook — a cluster of 1920s-era brick apartment buildings in the DeMun neighborhood (Millbrook Apartment 2).

adds.name: Eighth Church of Christ, Scientist
adds.description: A Christian Science church and Reading Room serving the Clayton/DeMun area.

adds.name: Our Lady of Lourdes Parish
adds.description: A Roman Catholic parish just west of the DeMun/Clayton line, with its permanent church dedicated in 1919; the parish also runs Our Lady of Lourdes School.

history.event: Our Lady of Lourdes parish is founded; the first Mass is celebrated by Father Francis J. O’Connor.
Archbishop John J. Glennon dedicates the permanent church (cornerstone laid 1917).

adds.name: Harbison House
adds.description: A named apartment building in the DeMun/Clayton area.

adds.name: Forsyth School
adds.description: An independent coeducational school (age 3 through grade 6) on the Wydown/Forsyth corridor, known for hands-on, creative learning across a campus of converted historic houses.

history.event: Mary Dunbar founds Forsyth School as a small preschool in a house leased from Unity Christ Church on Forsyth Boulevard.
Having added a grade level each year, Forsyth graduates its first sixth-grade class.

adds.name: DeMun Pointe
adds.description: A DeMun apartment building on Clayton Road, typical of the neighborhood’s defining 1920s three-story brick-and-limestone apartment blocks laid out under Henry Wright’s plan.

adds.name: Henry Wright Park
adds.description: A small neighborhood green in the heart of DeMun, named for landscape architect Henry Wright — whose 1920s "Garden City" plan for the district wove inward-facing streets and shared greens like this one between the brick apartment blocks.

adds.name: Washington University Catholic Student Center
adds.description: The Catholic campus ministry and chapel serving Washington University students, just off the Danforth campus.

adds.name: Chapel of Saint Timothy & Saint Titus
adds.description: The chapel of Concordia Seminary, part of the seminary’s 1926 Collegiate Gothic campus in the DeMun neighborhood — a Lutheran (LCMS) house of worship for the seminary community.

adds.name: St. Mark's Evangelical Lutheran Church
adds.description: A Lutheran congregation on Clayton Road in the Hi-Pointe/DeMun area.

adds.name: Our Lady of Lourdes School
adds.description: The parish school of Our Lady of Lourdes — a Catholic K–8 school on the Clayton/University City edge.

adds.name: Village House
adds.description: A named apartment building in the DeMun/Clayton area.

adds.name: Kaldi's Coffee Roasting Co.
amenities: House-roasted coffee — the original roasting café
A DeMun community gathering spot since 1994
adds.description: The original Kaldi's — where the St. Louis coffee company began. In 1994 two Mizzou journalism grads, Suzanne Langlois and Howard Lerner, quit their newspaper jobs and opened a café on this DeMun corner (a former travel agency, then a meditation center) with a mission "to create a place for people." A year in they began roasting their own beans in the shop; the operation grew into a roaster that now supplies 14 St. Louis-area cafés and more in Atlanta — since named the best coffee chain in the country. The flagship still pulls espresso on the corner where it all started.

history.event: Journalists Suzanne Langlois and Howard Lerner leave their newspaper jobs and open Kaldi's on the DeMun corner — a community café, "a place for people."
About a year in, they begin roasting their own coffee inside the café, then expand into a shuttered antique store behind it — the start of Kaldi's Coffee Roasting Co.
Now led by co-owner Tyler Zimmer, Kaldi's has grown to 14 St. Louis-area cafés (plus four in Atlanta) and been named the best coffee chain in the U.S. — the DeMun flagship still anchors the block.

adds.name: Louie
amenities: Wood-burning pizza oven imported from Italy
Free lot parking south of the building
adds.description: A warm, Italian-inspired neighborhood restaurant on DeMun from Matt McGuire (former service director at Niche Food Group), recognized by the James Beard Foundation for its hospitality. A wood-burning oven imported from Italy turns out slightly-thick Neapolitan-style pizzas; the kitchen also sends out antipasti, house pastas, and larger plates — the roast chicken is a St. Louis favorite. Cozy room, lively bar, and a first-come patio.

history.event: Matt McGuire opens Louie at 706 DeMun, in part of the former Jimmy's on the Park space — an Italian-inspired neighborhood joint with a wood-burning pizza oven brought over from Italy.
Louie earns James Beard Foundation recognition for outstanding hospitality, cementing its reputation as one of Clayton's most beloved restaurants.

adds.name: Sasha's Wine Bar
adds.description: The original Sasha's — a DeMun institution since 1993 and the anchor of Alan Richman's wine-bar family (sister to the neighboring Barrio). A 3,000-plus-bottle cellar drives an ever-changing list of wines by the glass, bottle, and side-by-side "Cellar Series" flights, paired with cheese and charcuterie boards, house chicken-liver pâté, prosciutto, and small plates. Buzzy, candlelit, and open late, with one of DeMun's liveliest patios.

history.event: Sasha's Wine Bar opens on DeMun Avenue, becoming a neighborhood cornerstone and the flagship of what grows into Alan Richman's family of St. Louis wine bars.
Barrio opens next door as a sister concept, extending the DeMun corner into a combined wine-bar-and-kitchen destination.

adds.name: Barrio
amenities: Full bar — craft cocktails, wine & rotating draft beer
Rotating desserts by an in-house French pastry chef
adds.description: A lively DeMun Avenue corner spot serving smash burgers, street tacos, and Latin-leaning sandwiches, with a full bar of craft cocktails, wine, and rotating local draft beer (plus a notably good zero-proof list). From restaurateur Alan Richman — sister to the neighboring Sasha’s Wine Bar — with a kitchen led by chef Dan Sammons. The cantilevered front windows open onto a dog-friendly sidewalk patio in good weather. Locally sourced ingredients; vegan "harvest shreds" available across the menu.

history.event: Owner Alan Richman and chef Dan Sammons open Barrio in the former DeMun Oyster Bar space (740 De Mun) — a tacos-tequila-and-tapas concept extending Sammons’ farmers-market "Backdoor Burritos," with street tacos, arepas, empanadas, enchiladas and Cuban sandwiches.
Barrio shifts to its now-signature "Burgers & Tacos" format — house smash burgers and street tacos alongside the original Latin plates.

adds.name: DeMun Oyster Bar
adds.description: Former oyster & seafood bar at 740 De Mun — permanently closed; the space is now Barrio.

adds.name: Clementine's Naughty & Nice Creamery
adds.description: St. Louis's original micro-creamery, from founder Tamara Keefe (Missouri's 2025 Small Business Person of the Year). Clementine's makes small-batch "Naughty" (boozy, 21+) and "Nice" (family-friendly, with vegan & dairy-free) ice creams — 24 chef-inspired flavors daily. Its Gooey Butter Cake, a nod to the St. Louis classic, was crowned by Oprah the "sexiest ice cream alive." The DeMun scoop shop is one of seven area parlors.

history.event: Tamara Keefe opens the first Clementine's — a 550-sq-ft, fresh-yet-vintage parlor in Lafayette Square — after cashing out her 401(k) to build an FDA-certified kitchen. Named for its "Naughty" (boozy) and "Nice" ice creams.
Clementine's opens its DeMun Avenue parlor at 730 De Mun as the brand expands across the St. Louis area.
Founder Tamara Keefe is named Missouri's Small Business Person of the Year.

adds.name: How Sweet Is This Candy Shoppe
adds.description: A tiny ~300-sq-ft candy shop packed with classic and new sweets.

adds.name: Seedz Cafe
adds.description: 100% vegan, nutrient-dense café — veggie burgers, chili-mac, tempeh Reubens, fresh-pressed juices and smoothies.

adds.name: Hi-Pointe Drive-In
adds.description: A cult-favorite burger stand at the foot of McCausland, from Mike Johnson and Adam Pritchett of Sugarfire Smokehouse. Built around the smash burger that had been Sugarfire's best-seller, it turns out inventive chef specials and boozy shakes from a converted 1980s drive-in — the owners kept the old name to honor the building and the Hi-Pointe neighborhood. A St. Louis burger destination and the flagship of a growing local chain.

history.event: Mike Johnson and Adam Pritchett (of Sugarfire Smokehouse) open Hi-Pointe Drive-In on Jan 5 in a converted 1980s drive-in at Clayton & McCausland — built around Sugarfire's award-winning smash burger, and keeping the old name to honor the building and neighborhood.
